title: Invocation orchestra: typed argument mapping and stream-flow helpers for polyglot SDKs
creator: Aisha Park
description: Problem: Our SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) expose function/tool calling primitives but lack a consistent, ergonomic approach to schema validation, cross-language argument mapping, and reliable streaming/resume semantics. This causes duplicated logic in customers' code, subtle bugs around type coercion, and fragile streaming recovery paths.
design_decision_summary: Provide an "invocation orchestra" consisting of: (1) a lightweight per-language adapter that performs runtime schema validation and coercion (opt-in strictness), (2) a canonical argument mapping layer that supports named and positional args and automatic type coercion policies, and (3) a streaming helper surface that unifies backpressure, cancelation, and resume tokens across runtimes. Use explicit idempotency tokens and sequence checkpoints for resumable streams. Prefer runtime validators that integrate with idiomatic toolchains: dataclasses/pydantic for Python, zod/io-ts optional validators for TypeScript, and generated validation tags for Go.
tradeoffs_and_notes:
- Strict validation reduces user errors but makes rollouts harder for permissive customers; default to lenient/coerce mode and allow strict=true.
- Streaming resume requires protocol-level sequence tokens which have compatibility implications; we will version tokens and fall back to full-body retry when tokens are unavailable.
- Implement adapters in SDKs rather than server-side to keep runtime costs predictable and let clients short-circuit obvious errors locally.
- Security: validation libraries must avoid arbitrary code execution (no eval). Audit required before GA.
implementation_plan:
1) Define a canonical JSON schema + lightweight mapping spec in docs (Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEV/pages/InvocationOrchestra).
2) Python adapter: dataclass + pydantic validator shim, async iterator helper supporting cancel tokens and 'resume_cursor'.
3) TypeScript adapter: optional zod schemas with a StreamingReadable<T> helper wrapping native ReadableStream for incremental function responses.
4) Go adapter: codegen for struct tags + ResumeToken handling; streaming uses channel-based chunked messages.
5) Cross-SDK compatibility tests and an interop harness (GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-invoke-harness).
6) Add examples in examples/typed-invoke for each language and publish SDK docs and migration guide.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a 'validate_and_invoke' helper that accepts a JSON schema and enforces it in the chosen mode (lenient|strict)
Examples for Python/TS/Go show identical observable behavior for named/positional args and streaming resumes
Streaming resume works end-to-end with sequence tokens in the interop harness (no lost tokens for 99% of test cases)
Retries use idempotency tokens and follow jittered backoff; integration tests show no duplicate side-effects for idempotent operations
Security review completed and dependencies audited for validators before release
